expected_behavior_change: MFP device identity remains stable across reload while authorization always restarts UNKNOWN until formal readback.
Only a formal auth authority response can create an in-memory authenticated staff session.
Expired, revoked, unknown, mismatched or under-permissioned actions fail before Store Kernel submit.
MFP Pad and MFP Mobile share the same security port and existing A1 Store Kernel port semantics.
The minimal A2 harness exposes device, login, staff, expiry, logout and permission-denied states without persisting PIN or session authority.
non_goals: No production auth endpoint or Store Kernel binding.
No Store Kernel, Pricing, Order, Payment, Fulfillment, Print, Customer or Keeta authority change.
No Builder or OTA protocol change.
No merge, deploy, cutover or legacy SMM decommission.
